subject: Dedicated capacity: priority routing & fallback proposal (Polaris AI)
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@polaris.ai>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: ops@polaris.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — priority routing / throughput guarantees

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like Redwood's Dedicated offering but need to lock down how priority routing and fallback behavior will work for our tail-sensitive latency workloads. Two specific asks: 

1) When our reserved pool is saturated, can requests from Polaris be routed to a lower-cost shared fallback model without dropping below our 95th percentile latency target (200ms)? We need clear guarantees for how often a fallback would be used and what latency uplift to expect.

2) We send a mix of short chat requests and periodic long-context embeddings. Is there a documented queue-priority policy that lets short, latency-sensitive requests jump ahead of long batch jobs within our reservation? If not, we need an exception or carve-out to avoid head-of-line blocking during scheduled batch windows.

I attached a small sample of our 1-week tail distribution (polaris-throughput-sample.json). Can Redwood provide a proposed exception or amendment to the Dedicated SLA that covers: priority routing for p95-sensitive traffic, a defined fallback model and its latency profile, and observable metrics we can use to audit compliance?

We are on a tight procurement timeline (target sign by Apr 20). Appreciate any quick clarity.

—Jordan
Jordan Park
Head of Platform, Polaris AI
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@polaris.ai>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — priority routing / throughput guarantees

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks and the sample. High level response: yes, we support policy-driven fallback routing and we can propose a carve-out that prioritizes short p95 traffic inside your reserved pool. A few quick notes: 

- Fallbacks: our standard fallback is to a compatible quantized variant of the pinned model hosted in the shared tier. Typical p95 uplift varies by workload; for chat-like short requests we've observed 1.4–1.8x latency at p95 vs dedicated (depends on batch mixing).
- Priority: we have queue classes (short/interactive vs long/batch) available for Dedicated customers; however, default configs favor throughput. We can add a queue-preemption rule for Polaris that promotes requests tagged as latency-sensitive.

I'll loop in Marcus (runtime product) and Laura (contracts) to propose specific SLA language and measurement hooks (tracing tags, p95 on route, fallback counters). If you can confirm the exact p95 SLO you want enforced and whether you require fallback to be rate-limited or avoided entirely once a threshold is hit, we can draft an amendment today.

Sofia Ivanova
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@polaris.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — priority routing / throughput guarantees

Jordan/Sofia — quick technical sketch.

Proposal for Polaris priority carve-out (runtime behavior):
- Traffic classification: Polaris will tag latency-sensitive requests with header X-Polaris-Priority: high or via route mapping in the Redwood Console.
- Queueing: high-priority requests are assigned to an interactive queue with strict headroom. Interactive queue preempts batching slots up to a configurable ratio (default 20% of pool tokens).
- Fallback policy: if all interactive capacity is saturated for >60s, requests are diverted to a fallback variant. We can cap fallback usage to a maximum of 5% of total requests in any rolling 5-minute window — beyond that, Redwood will notify and throttle non-critical batch work to preserve Polaris p95.
- Observability: expose per-route metrics: interactive_p95_ms, fallback_rate, queue_depth_by_class. We'll add an alert that fires if fallback_rate > 2% for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows.

Attachment: redwood-sla-diff.pdf (proposed SLA amendment snippet).

This is intentionally conservative. If Polaris wants stricter guarantees (lower fallback cap or shorter diversion window), legal/finance will need to sign off on added credit/penalty terms.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Runtime Product
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — priority routing / throughput guarantees

Looping in for contracts. Internal note: Marcus' technical sketch looks good but we need to be explicit about measurement windows and remedies. Proposed contract language to offer Polaris: 

- Commitment: Dedicated pool reserved for Polaris with interactive p95 target of 200ms for tagged requests when fallback_rate <= 5% in a 5-minute window.
- Remedy: If fallback_rate > 5% for two consecutive 5-minute windows and p95 > 200ms, Redwood issues a credit equal to 5% of monthly Dedicated fee for that day per incident.
- Auditability: Redwood will provide a daily CSV export with per-route metrics and a shared dashboard link. Polaris may run quarterly spot audits (read-only) via a support token.

Can we approve offering the 5% cap + credit remedy for this deal if Polaris signs by Apr 20? Finance will need the revenue schedule and the SLA appendix.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@polaris.ai>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@polaris.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — priority routing / throughput guarantees

Thanks, team — the proposal looks reasonable. Two quick asks before we sign: 

1) Please shorten the diversion trigger to 30s (instead of 60s) and reduce the allowed fallback cap to 3% in any 5-minute window. Those changes reflect our tail sensitivity and will keep user-facing p95 tight.
2) Provide the initial daily CSV export as a shared BigQuery table rather than CSV if possible — that will simplify our audits.

We are ready to proceed once the SLA appendix reflects those two changes. I've asked our legal to expect a Hellosign package.

Jordan
Jordan Park
Head of Platform, Polaris AI
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — priority routing & fallback proposal (Polaris AI)

Internal follow-up: legal and finance reviewed Polaris' counter. We can accept the 30s diversion trigger and 3% fallback cap but will require: 
- A small premium (1.5x unit price for interactive tokens during peak hours) to offset added preemption risk, and
- A one-way SLA credit cap: maximum credit per month capped at 10% of monthly Dedicated fee.

Action items: Sofia, send updated SLA appendix with Marcus' runtime parameters and the adjusted financial terms. Include the BigQuery share link option and attach the Hellosign package link. I'll coordinate with Finance to finalize the revenue schedule for the deal (deal id POL-2027-0410).

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
